text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected in hosted-runtime-prod — sudden KV cache memory spike on worker-pool-9. Error rate increasing for text-generation endpoints. Auto-scaler reporting OOM risk. Pager sent to on-call.

alex: acknowledged, I'm on it. grabbing recent metrics + traces.

maria: getting customer impact now — support queue shows 3 customers with timeouts. which endpoints?

support-karen: customers #alpha and #gamma seeing 504s on /v1/generate, #beta has degraded latency. all reports started ~12:41 UTC.

alex: looking at kvcache metrics — key_count doubled in last 3m, kv_windows size per-session jumped to ~18MB from 2MB. looks like runaway context windows.

eng-runtime-lead: any recent releases? batching or prefetch changes in last deploy?

alex: deploy-bot shows a config push 12:35 UTC: continuous-batching v2 enabled with aggressive prefetch factor=3 for hosted tier.

sre_jordan: that matches. prefetch factor ramped in prod can cause kv growth with long prompts. suggestion: throttle prefetch or set max_kv_window_bytes per-session temporarily.

maria: propose emergency throttle: set prefetch factor back to 1 and cap kv window to 8MB for hosted-runtime-prod. will that be safe for latency?

eng-runtime-lead: yes, temporary cap will increase token compute slightly but avoids OOM. we should also disable cross-request prefetching for now.

alex: preparing hotfix patch. applying change to runtime-config service in prod region a.

alex: command: ```
# emergency config update
curl -X POST "https://config.internal/api/v1/update" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"service":"runtime","env":"hosted-prod","patch":{"prefetch_factor":1,"max_kv_window_bytes":8388608,"cross_request_prefetch":false}}'
```

deploy-bot: Deploy job started: runtime-config-update/2387654321. Canary on pool-9-worker-3.

incident-bot: Pager escalated to on-call. Status: mitigation in progress.

sre_jordan: canary applied. watching memory.

alex: memory on canary dropped from 92% to 36% within 45s. KV key_count stopped climbing.

maria: checking customer reports — support queue shows alpha & gamma recovered, beta latency improving.

support-karen: confirmed, customers reporting success. I'll send interim note to affected customers: brief RC and ETA for full fix.

eng-runtime-lead: roll the change to full prod. do a staggered rollout across regions to avoid load spikes.

deploy-bot: Canary succeeded. Rolling to region-a nodes.

alex: rollout to region-a complete. memory stable. now progressing region-b.

sre_jordan: adding a short-term autoscaling buffer to avoid thrash while rollout finishes: scale-out-threshold set to 70% for 10m.

product-ops: are there ongoing SLA violations we need to log for customers? track minutes for incident timeline.

maria: yes — initial impact window 12:41–12:46 UTC for majority, partial until 12:49 for a few. I'll capture detailed timestamps after we consolidate logs.

eng-runtime-lead: root-cause hypothesis: recent continuous-batching prefetch change increased cross-request KV population; certain customers with very long prompts (system + context amplification) caused per-session KV explosion leading to memory pressure. We'll treat this as regression introduced by aggressive prefetch defaults.

alex: creating a follow-up task: revert aggressive prefetch in canary branch, add safety knobs: global max_kv_window_bytes default 8MB and per-customer override via dedicated capacity.

sre_jordan: also recommend adding realtime alert for rapid kv growth: >2x key_count in 2m for a worker -> auto-throttle prefetch per-worker.

support-karen: will send an impacted-customer message: short apology, mitigation done, ask if they saw any data loss.

product-ops: schedule a postmortem tomorrow 0900 PT; owners: alex (mitigation), eng-runtime-lead (fix + rollout), maria (incident timeline), support-karen (customer comms), sre_jordan (alerts + runbook update).

maria: adding note — we saw one customer using concatenated system messages that created a prefix amplification loop. include eval tests for long prompt scenarios in next release gating.

alex: logs and flamegraphs saved to /incidents/2387654321/artifacts. I'll attach a shortened log snippet here for the postmortem.

alex: ```
# excerpt
worker=pool-9 pid=4321 kv_bytes=18753216 key_count=2419
alloc_trace: prefetch_module:expand_keys -> kv_insert_batch -> kv_reserve
```

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. No active page.

maria: closing loop on timeline and customer notes. thanks everyone for fast response. :thumbsup:

product-ops: postmortem invite sent and incident chronicle created. we'll follow up with action items and ETA for the config defaults change.

sre_jordan: I'll file runbook update with the emergency throttle procedure we used.

support-karen: sent customer updates. one asked for root-cause; hold until postmortem.

alex: moving to cleanup — watch for any regressions while we re-enable prefetch in a controlled A/B test that includes KV caps.

eng-runtime-lead: planned next steps: 1) permanent default cap, 2) add per-worker auto-throttle rule, 3) improve canary tests for long prompt workloads. ETA: code + rollout plan by EOD tomorrow.

maria: thanks all. marking incident resolved in channel once artifacts + timeline are finalized.
